issues.item: Triggers: Victim Similarity: People who look similar to the victims
issues.explanation: For a mugging/robbery trauma, 'people who look similar to the victims' is clinically incoherent because the patient is the victim; a plausible trigger would be people resembling the perpetrator(s) or contextual robbery cues. As written, this item conflicts with the trauma type.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: Feeling dirty/contaminated is not impossible after robbery, but in this profile it is hard to reconcile with the rest of the selected items, which otherwise center on danger, self-blame, and moral injury rather than sexual violation or disgust-based trauma themes. This makes the appraisal set clinically inconsistent with the trauma context.

For a mugging/robbery trauma, 'Being naked' as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless there was a stripping/sexual humiliation element, which is not suggested elsewhere in the profile. The other trigger items point to perpetrator proximity and assault cues, making this vulnerability trigger clinically incongruent with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Violated Values: I acted in ways that go against who I am
issues.explanation: 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' implies morally troubling behaviour during the event, but the rest of the profile reflects victim-focused danger, self-blame, and mistrust rather than any specific morally injurious action. In a mugging/robbery context this item is difficult to justify without corroborating memory/appraisal content about the patient's own behaviour.

vignette: Leilani's life changed forever on that fateful evening when she was mugged while walking home from work. As an accountant, she often found herself lost in thought, and her mind would wander to numbers and spreadsheets. But on that particular night, the sound of footsteps behind her shattered her concentration. She tried to quicken her pace, but before she knew it, a hand had reached out and grabbed her purse. The vivid memory of the taste of fear still lingered in Leilani's mouth whenever she thought about that moment. Her body would tense up, assuming the same defensive position as when the mugger approached her. The more she ruminated on what could have been done to prevent it - if only she had taken a different route or walked faster - the more her mind seemed to convince her that it was all her fault. She started to believe that the world was indeed a treacherous place, and that she, as a person, was somehow responsible for attracting danger. As Leilani tried to navigate her daily routine, certain triggers would set off this chain of thoughts. Hearing footsteps behind her or being touched unexpectedly by someone would send her into a panic. She became increasingly paranoid, constantly scanning her surroundings for potential threats. Even in the safety of her own home, she couldn't shake off the feeling that something was about to go terribly wrong. When her husband tried to reassure her that everything would be okay, Leilani found it impossible to trust his words. Her mind kept wandering back to the moment when her purse was snatched, and how she had frozen in fear. She began to wonder if there was something fundamentally wrong with her - a flaw in her character that made her more susceptible to harm. Leilani's maladaptive coping strategies started to take hold as she tried to deal with these overwhelming emotions. She would deliberately try to dissociate herself from the memories, attempting to blank out or leave her body whenever they resurfaced. However, this only led to further feelings of disconnection and confusion. Her ruminations about what had happened began to consume her thoughts, making it difficult for her to focus on anything else. Her negative appraisals - that she was somehow flawed and that the world was a perilous place - started to feed into each other, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of fear and anxiety. She became convinced that even when others told her she was safe, there must be something lurking beneath the surface waiting to pounce. As Leilani struggled to come to terms with what had happened, her work as an accountant began to suffer. Simple tasks like balancing spreadsheets or meeting deadlines started to feel daunting. Her relationships also suffered - she became increasingly withdrawn and isolated, unable to shake off the feeling that she was living in a constant state of threat. Leilani's story is one of entrapment in this cycle of fear and self-blame. She feels trapped by her memories and unable to escape the narrative that has taken hold of her mind - that she is flawed and the world is a treacherous place. Her journey towards recovery will require her to confront these negative appraisals head-on, learning to challenge them and develop more constructive coping strategies in their place. The memory of that fateful evening continues to haunt Leilani, its vividness refusing to fade with time. As she navigates the complexities of her own mind, it's clear that this traumatic event has left an indelible mark on her life - one that will take time and effort to overcome.
